title: Keeping Your Kin Close
note: A ruler holds his relatives close so that they don’t leave him. Having spoken of those who do his work, he turns here to the rest of his circle.

couplets.plain: Only kin go on cherishing old ties even when you have lost everything.
couplets.pm: The habit of staying with a man when his wealth is gone and he is poor, and of fondly recalling the old bond, is found only among kin. The old bond is what he did for them in better days. Everyone else cuts their ties the moment he loses his means.

links.quote: Only kin go on cherishing old ties

couplets.plain: If you have kin whose fondness never ends, they will bring you many gains that go on sprouting.
couplets.pm: If a man finds kin whose loving-kindness doesn’t end, they give him many kinds of wealth that never stop branching. “If he finds” shows how rare this is. Unending sets them apart from enemies within. The many are the six limbs of a kingdom, which keep branching because many people raise them together.

links.quote: kin whose fondness never ends
links.reason: Sees gains that keep sprouting in the unending fondness of one’s kin.

couplets.plain: A life with no sharing of hearts is like a broad tank filling with water and no bank around it.
couplets.pm: The life of a man whose heart doesn’t mingle with his kin is like a wide tank filled with water and no banks. Kin comes from the subject of the chapter. Life means the wealth that supports it. Mingling comes from talking over each other’s state. The wealth of a man with no kin has no one to hold it, and it flows away.

links.quote: no sharing of hearts
links.reason: Without closeness of heart, a life runs off like water with no bank to hold it.

links.quote: a broad tank filling with water and no bank around it

couplets.plain: The reward of having wealth is to live so that your kin gather round you.
couplets.pm: What a man gains from gaining wealth is to embrace his kin and live surrounded by them. It is called the reward of wealth because such conduct lets him rule without enemies.

links.quote: live so that your kin gather round you

couplets.plain: If you can give and speak sweetly, you will be surrounded by kin, rank upon rank.
couplets.pm: If a man is able to give his kin what they need and to speak sweet words, he is surrounded by many kinds of kin who follow one from another. “Able” shows that doing both in the right measure is hard. Following means the kin of kin, and their kin in turn, bound to him through each other.

links.quote: surrounded by kin, rank upon rank
speak sweetly
If you can give
links.reason: Giving is the other half of what brings relatives near.

couplets.plain: No one on this wide earth has more people at their side than a great giver who doesn’t cherish anger.
couplets.pm: If a man gives greatly and doesn’t favour anger, no one in this world has kin like his. Great giving means giving so that not one of them goes poor. Not favouring anger means not going beyond measure in the belief that a ruler needs it.

links.quote: a great giver
doesn’t cherish anger
No one on this wide earth has more people at their side

couplets.plain: The crow doesn’t hide its food. It calls the others and eats. Gains come only to those with a nature like that.
couplets.pm: When crows find food they don’t hide it but call their kind and eat with them. The gains that come through kin belong only to those of that nature, who see that their kin enjoy all that they enjoy. The gains are having no enemies, great wealth and the like. Wealth comes to them along with righteousness and pleasure.

links.quote: It calls the others and eats
links.reason: Holds up the crow that calls its fellows to eat as the pattern for those who would prosper.

couplets.plain: If a ruler looks on people not all alike but each by their rank, many will live by that regard.
couplets.pm: If a ruler doesn’t regard everyone alike but regards each according to his fitness, many kin will live by him for that honour and never leave. He rules out treating all alike because the higher ones would go, and he calls for ranked regard so that all will stay.

links.quote: each by their rank
If a ruler looks on people not all alike

couplets.plain: Those who were your own and left you will come back as kin, once the cause of the rift is gone.
couplets.pm: When those who were his own leave him for some cause, they come back and are kin once that cause no longer lies with him. The cause is such things as the ruler going astray or doing what they hate. Kin have loving-kindness by nature, so a break made by circumstance ends with its cause. No wooing is needed, and they return to what they were.

links.quote: once the cause of the rift is gone
will come back as kin
Those who were your own and left you will come back

couplets.plain: When someone who left comes back for a reason, a ruler should meet that reason, think it through and take them in.
couplets.pm: When a kinsman who left for no cause comes back for a cause, the ruler should do what he came for, then consider him and take him in. If he doesn’t, the man leaves again and joins the enemy. He left without loving-kindness and came back with a motive, so he needs thought. Those who left to do harm and those who come back to do good are both to be taken in.

links.quote: take them in
someone who left comes back for a reason
think it through and take them in

ideaLinks.quote: If you can give and speak sweetly, you will be surrounded by kin
speak sweetly, you will be surrounded by kin
many gains that go on sprouting
ideaLinks.reason: Unending fondness among kin brings gains that keep on sprouting.
